delivery every time from the widest selection of grocers, we believe managing the inventory ourselves for third-party grocers is important. This is why we started our DashMart project five years ago, first learning how to do this by holding our own inventory, and now managing thousands of high-quality products from Giant Eagle, Albertsons, and others. When we manage inventory ourselves, we achieve 99%+ fulfillment accuracy. 8 We also deliver more than 10 minutes faster on average, 9 because the warehouse environment is optimized for delivery whereas a grocery store was never set up for delivery. In addition to faster delivery, managing the inventory ourselves gives us the potential to reduce the cost of fulfillment, and lower costs enable us to reinvest into more value for consumers. Managing inventory inside a warehouse is a fixed cost business. Scale is a necessary (though insufficient) input into helping lower costs. This is one of the reasons we’re attracted to Instacart, as it adds scale that is unique to our network. Over the past 14 years, Instacart has built a great brand that serves millions of consumers. Hence, we believe that combining our reach will enable the best possible logistics and software infrastructure to produce the best possible grocery delivery experience for grocers, consumers, Shoppers, and advertising partners. We expect this to be true on Day 1 (after close), as the combined reach will increase density across the grocery store network, helping increase delivery speed, lower fulfillment costs, and provide greater earning opportunities for Shoppers. As we have historically done, we expect to reinvest a portion of the improved network efficiencies into creating a better experience for all audiences. We’ve done this both with our U.S. restaurant marketplace, where our reinvestments into product innovation have continued to generate durable growth, and in our acquired businesses outside of the U.S. Most recently, we demonstrated this investment philosophy and approach at Deliveroo, which in Q3 2026, saw Total Orders grow at twice the Y/Y rate it did in Q3 2025 (pre-acquisition). To this end, we see a multi-year path to $500 million or more of annual synergies, net of investments. We expect to invest more than 100% of total synergies in the first year after close, followed by positive net synergies in year two and beyond.
